headline: Compumedics' Somfit disposable sleep device is months away from US commercial launch, targeting a 4-million-plus annual home sleep testing market.
reasoning: Compumedics has already begun commercialising the reusable version of Somfit in the US and is a few months away from making its disposable version commercially available. The device represents a strategic shift from low-volume, high-value capital equipment to high-volume, lower-value consumable devices. Somfit's competitive advantage is its direct EEG channels via forehead attachment, which differentiates it in the US home sleep testing market. Beyond home testing, Somfit is gaining traction in the pharmaceutical clinical trial market, where drugs must assess their impact on sleep, with Compumedics now embedded in 3–4 of the largest contract research organisations.
quote: The company has traditionally sold capital equipment, relatively low values and like low volumes, high values, whereas some 50 is a relatively low value device but extremely high volume. So we have committed to manufacturing now and have signed those contracts. So we're, uh, maybe a few months away from having that commercially available in the US, but it is very close indeed... we see a continuing significant opportunity into the home sleeve testing market in America, where there are 4 million plus studies done per annum and some 50 device has EEG channels because we attach the device to the forehead. So we get those channels directly from the device, which is a competitive advantage in the market there.
episode_title: Compumedics dreams bigger as sleep diagnostics scale

headline: Sees continued MEG device growth opportunities in China and is pursuing a deal to re-enter the North American market with dual-helmet pediatric technology
reasoning: The MEG business generated $9.7 million in FY26 revenue, predominantly from China, compared to nil the prior year. Compumedics is now pursuing a deal in North America with its dual-helmet MEG system, which includes both adult and pediatric helmets — a key differentiator versus competitors who rely on adult-only helmets for all patients. The pediatric helmet improves measurement outcomes for children, which the CFO described as a meaningful clinical and commercial advantage. Management indicated a deal announcement in the North American market was anticipated in the near term.
quote: We're looking to, uh, close the deal in the not too distant future. And that will, uh, get us back into the North American market with our dual helmet technology. Uh, the key differentiator for us against our competitors in the Meg is that we have a pediatric helmet as well as an adult helmet, uh, which, uh, greatly improves, uh, the outcomes of the measurements in the Meg system. Uh, with children going into a pediatric sized helmet, as opposed to using a adult helmet to try and and get, uh, correct readings off of children.

headline: Compumedics CFO highlights record FY26 results and targets continued double-digit revenue growth in FY27, with EBITDA expected to grow faster than revenue.
reasoning: Compumedics delivered record full-year FY26 revenue of $60.3 million, up 19%, while returning to profitability and generating $6.6 million in operating cash flow. The two key growth engines were the Nexus 360 enterprise sleep diagnostics software, which grew to over $10 million in revenue from virtually nothing three years ago, and the MEG business, which contributed $9.7 million in revenue compared to nothing the prior year. Management is targeting double-digit revenue growth in FY27 with EBITDA growing faster than revenue, supported by cost efficiencies and a strong order book. The CFO acknowledged some investor scepticism but attributed the share price weakness to a need to build a longer track record and communicate the story more broadly.
quote: From our point of view, uh, the key results were the improving profitability of the group and the improving cash generation. Obviously, record revenues are $60.3 million. We're critical to driving that earnings improvement and the cash flow improvement. And the two big factors driving the revenue growth were our software product on the sleep diagnostics side of the business, which improved with our Nexus 360, uh, enterprise system to ten point just over $10 million of revenue from virtually nothing three years ago. And our Meg business, where we had $9.7 million of revenue in this year compared to nothing last year. So both those are the growth engines of the business moving forward.
episode_title: Compumedics dreams bigger as sleep diagnostics scale
